spots.name: Currant Mountain
spots.tip: A notable summit. Check the road and trail first; first and last light on high ground is the reason to go, and it's often the subject from below. Summit 3,492 m (11,457 ft).

spots.name: Troy Peak
spots.tip: A notable summit. Check the road and trail first; first and last light on high ground is the reason to go, and it's often the subject from below. Summit 3,336 m (10,945 ft).

spots.name: Adaven
spots.tip: A landmark with history. Low light brings out texture; check opening hours if it's fenced.

spots.name: Wayne E Kirch Wildlife Management Area
spots.tip: Wildlife is most active in the first two hours after sunrise. Stay on trails, use your car as a blind on auto routes and give animals space.

spots.name: Railroad Valley WMA: Lockes Ranch
spots.tip: eBird birding hotspot with 119 species recorded. Birds are most active in the first two hours after sunrise; recent sightings at ebird.org/hotspot/L875725.

spots.name: Moorman Spring
spots.tip: Steam reads best in cold air at first light. Check access rules; many springs are on private or tribal land.

spots.name: Blackrock Summit
spots.tip: A mountain pass: easy high ground by car. Fog often fills the valleys on either side at sunrise; check winter road conditions.
